subject: Clarifying processing regions, subprocessors, and cross-border transfers - DataBridge Q&A
messages:
From: Maria Lopez <maria.lopez@databridge.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 20 Jan 2026 08:15:00 -0800
Subject: Question: where is customer data processed and which subprocessors are involved?

Hi Stephanie,

Thanks for the demo last week. As we prepare our procurement paperwork and escalate to InfoSec, we need a succinct Q&A about where DataBridge customer inference data is processed, which subprocessors have access to prompt/request data (and for what purposes), and whether any cross-border transfers occur for hosted or dedicated modes. Specifically: 

1) Which cloud regions or Redwood-managed datacenters process tokens for the hosted API? Are there guarantees for EU-only processing?
2) Do any subprocessors (cloud providers, logging/analytics, observability vendors) have the ability to see plaintext prompts or outputs? If so, which ones and under what contractual limits?
3) For Dedicated and Private deployments, what changes (networking, key management, data-at-rest) should we note?

Can you send a short written summary and any supporting inventory CSV or diagram we can attach to our security review?

Thanks,
Maria Lopez
Sr. Procurement Manager
DataBridge Systems

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
To: Maria Lopez <maria.lopez@databridge.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 20 Jan 2026 11:02:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Question: where is customer data processed and which subprocessors are involved?

Hi Maria — great question and happy to provide a concise summary for your security packet. I've attached a short PDF (redwood-datapath-summary.pdf) and a CSV export of our current subprocessor inventory (dp-subprocessors.csv). High-level answers below; Vivek (legal) and Dylan (solutions/infra) are looped in for any technical or contractual clarifications.

1) Hosted API processing regions:
- Primary processing occurs in cloud regions in the US (us-west-2, us-east-1) and EU (eu-west-1). For hosted customers that require EU-only residency, we offer an EU residency option: requests routed and processed exclusively in EU regions and logged to EU-bound storage. This is a configuration during onboarding and is reflected in the customer tenancy settings.

2) Subprocessor access and duties:
- Our inventory (attached) lists cloud providers (AWS, GCP), a managed logging provider (LogStream Ltd.), observability backend (TraceKeep), and a limited set of monitoring/ops partners.
- By default, cloud provider staff do not have access to plaintext prompts/outputs beyond what is necessary for infra operations. We use encryption at rest and in transit; for hosted customers data is encrypted with per-tenant keys managed by Redwood KMS integrated with cloud KMS.
- Subprocessors with any potential access are contractually restricted (NDA + DPA clauses), have least-privilege roles, and we require subprocessors to have SOC 2 Type II or equivalent. The CSV includes the purpose column (compute, storage, logging, telemetry) and whether they process request/response content.

3) Dedicated / Private changes:
- Dedicated: runs on a reserved pool in customer-owned cloud account or Redwood-managed but isolated tenancy. Network isolation, VPC peering, and customer-controlled storage buckets recommended. Keys can be customer-managed (BYOK) or Redwood-managed.
- Private (VPC/on-prem): control plane remains customer-controlled; on-prem variant keeps all inference within your network; no Redwood-hosted persistent copies unless explicitly enabled. Access controls are enforced via our IAM + customer firewall policies.

A few notes on cross-border transfers:
- For hosted with default routing, requests may route to the nearest available region to meet latency/cost policies; this can result in cross-border processing unless residency is selected.
- EU-residency customers have data processed and stored within EU regions; backups and logs are retained in-region by default and any cross-border replication requires explicit contractual exception.

Attachments: redwood-datapath-summary.pdf (diagram + summary), dp-subprocessors.csv (inventory + purposes), SOC2 report stub for reviewers.

Next steps: I can produce a short one-page bullet summary tailored for legal (if helpful) and Vivek can provide contract language for DPAs/residency SLAs.

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>

Hi Maria and team — Vivek from Redwood Legal here. Quick answers to the InfoSec bullets below; I'm happy to follow up with formal DPA excerpts or redlines.

1) Observability telemetry: by design we do not route full plaintext prompts/outputs to external observability vendors. TraceKeep and LogStream receive metrics, request identifiers, and truncated payload hashes for debugging/latency analysis. Any textual sampling is opt-in and requires an explicit customer configuration and agreement. We also offer a redact-by-default setting that strips prompt/output text from logs.

2) EU residency guarantee: yes — for customers that select EU residency we include a residency SLA in the customer contract. That clause states logs, backups, and processing will remain within the designated EU regions; cross-border transfer is only permitted under narrow exceptions (court order, customer opt-in, or mutually agreed operational reasons) and will be subject to notification windows. We can provide the exact contract language; we generally rely on SCCs and, where applicable, adequacy decisions as legal mechanisms.

3) Dedicated + BYOK support access: when BYOK is enabled and keys are customer-controlled (not escrowed by Redwood), Redwood support cannot decrypt customer data without an explicit temporary credential or key release from the customer. For Dedicated where keys are Redwood-managed, support may be able to access data under strict internal controls and documented access requests — we can surface those logs. We recommend an operational runbook defining emergency procedures and a short-term key escrow mechanism if you require Redwood supportability with minimal friction.

Action items:
- Stephanie: I'll draft DPA snippets for the residency SLA, subprocessor notification (we typically provide 30 days notice for significant new subprocessors and immediate notice for any incidents impacting content access), and a section covering telemetry redaction options.
- Dylan: please confirm the technical details about truncation/obfuscation in logs (how sampling is gated) and add a brief note for the one-pager.

Happy to jump on a quick call if that helps expedite.
